sources.title: Oracle Database Concepts: Introduction to Oracle Database
sources.notes: Official database concepts documentation; cited for tables, entities, attributes, and row instances.

evidence.quote: A table describes an entity such as employees.
A column identifies an attribute of the entity described by the table
A row identifies an instance of the entity.

sources.title: Database normalization description
sources.notes: Microsoft's archived relational database design article; cited for relationships between tables and separating repeating groups.

evidence.quote: Normalization is the process of organizing data in a database. It includes creating tables and establishing relationships between those tables according to rules designed both to protect the data and to make the database more flexible by eliminating redundancy and inconsistent dependency.

sources.notes: Official PostgreSQL tutorial for SELECT queries, result columns, and WHERE qualifications.

evidence.quote: An SQL SELECT statement is used to do this.
A query can be “qualified” by adding a WHERE clause that specifies which rows are wanted.

sources.title: PostgreSQL Tutorial: Joins Between Tables
sources.notes: Official PostgreSQL tutorial for combining rows through join queries and pairing expressions.

evidence.quote: Queries that access multiple tables (or multiple instances of the same table) at one time are called join queries.
They combine rows from one table with rows from a second table, with an expression specifying which rows are to be paired.
